__doc: Canonical role vocabulary for the SGS cloning pipeline. THE source of truth for the `roles` table — db_lookup._migrate_roles_table() seeds from this file on module load (INSERT OR REPLACE + DELETE-NOT-IN two-way sync).
__why: Was a hardcoded Python dict of 21 entries while the live DB held 29. The 8 extra were each added by a one-off migration that wrote the DB row and never back-wrote the seed, so a rebuild silently lost them. That is the decay class Phase 0/1 exists to end, and a hardcoded routing dict also breaches R-31-1. Captured from live 2026-08-02.
a11y-text: Accessibility metadata: a screen-reader-facing string (aria-label, alt on a decorative image, a nav landmark label). SEEDED FOR DOCUMENTATION, NOT ROUTING (Bean, 2026-08-04). Classification is deliberately 'styling-behaviour' so these rows are EXCLUDED from the content walk: they are content in the everyday sense, but nothing in the converter reads a draft's aria-label into an attr (the only aria-label consumer is field_extractors' STAR-rating count), and marking them content-bearing would let the walk lift screen-reader text into visible clone content. Do NOT use 'image-alt' for these -- that role means alt text for a SIBLING image-object attr, resolved via block_attributes.alt_companion_attr and consumed by the image arm (db_lookup.py:2611-2636, walk.py:485); an aria-label with no companion image would feed a consumer expecting one. This role exists so a future agent reading the DB knows what these attrs ARE rather than finding a bare NULL and assuming something is missing.
behaviour: Excludes the attr from the content-bearing walk (FR-31-2.2) -- equivalent_block_for()/content_attrs_for_identity() deliberately skip role='behaviour' rows (converter/walk.py:405-408). Real consumer: style_preset_attrs_for_identity() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:3518-3553) mirrors a nested identity's inheritStyle onto the parent's OWN behaviour-role string attr (e.g. sgs/product-card.ctaStyle mirroring a nested sgs/button's --primary/--secondary modifier); also grouped into the BEM-modifier probe at db_lookup.py:4889-4896 alongside select-from-enum/enum-class-probe. MISCLASSIFICATION FOUND + FIXED 2026-08-04: `placeholder` on 11 sgs/form-field-* blocks + sgs/filter-search + sgs/product-search carried role='behaviour', which silently dropped a draft's placeholder text (it never reaches the content walk) -- changed to role='content' (see the 'content' entry) since a placeholder is client-authored text, not a style preset.
boolean-visibility: A boolean editor-only toggle (e.g. core/navigation.overlay, sgs/modal.closeOnOverlay, sgs/team-member.overlayHover). NO consumer in the converter -- no code anywhere branches on the literal 'boolean-visibility'; classification alone (styling-behaviour) keeps it out of the content walk. A draft's HTML/CSS carries no signal a boolean toggle could be lifted from, so the absence of a resolver is expected, not a gap.
color: Marks an attr whose value is a colour (design-token slug / hex / rgb() / named colour). Consumer: attr_is_colour_role() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1075-1103) is the sole legitimate gate for routing an OUTER/CONTENT-layer value through colour serialisation (extract_token_or_hex) instead of the generic string/numeric branches -- deliberately implemented as a SQL WHERE clause, not a Python `role == "color"` compare, so the no_slug_literal AST gate never sees it. Also feeds the px/string CSS-kind classifier _kind_for() (db_lookup.py:1955-1956).
colour-gradient: Marks a background-image gradient/url attr (property_suffixes suffix='Gradient', css_property='background-image'). Consumer: _kind_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1962-1963) resolves it to CSS kind 'string' (a raw `url(...)`/gradient() value); converter/resolvers/outer_box.py:51-57 resolves the block's own Gradient-suffix attr when a background-image declaration needs a destination.

colour-gradient.excludes_reason: The contract's value IS the raw url()/gradient() string -- a boolean cannot hold it. Found live 2026-08-05 (D497 follow-up, TIER 3.7): sgs/container|cta-section|hero|trust-bar.overlayGradient is a plain ON/OFF toggle (its sibling overlayGradientFrom/To strings carry the actual colour-gradient value) -- the role belonged on the siblings, not the toggle. See assign-canonical.py TIER 3.7.

colour-text: Seeded in the role vocabulary but currently UNUSED -- zero block_attributes rows carry it (verified 2026-08-04: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM block_attributes WHERE role='colour-text'` = 0) and no converter code reads the literal 'colour-text'. A role nothing reads: a genuine finding, not yet wired to any attr or resolver.
content: Generic content-bearing text marker. Treated as a first-class ALIAS of 'text-content' throughout extraction: converter/walk.py:270-274 (_typed_value_for_role), converter/services/field_extractors.py:172-184 (extract_field_value), converter/db/db_lookup.py:5228,5257 (primary_content_attr), converter/resolvers/scalar_content.py:121,164 (lift_scalar_content). Both roles are content-bearing per _content_bearing_roles() (db_lookup.py:3744) and route identically through the Tier-A canonical_slot join in equivalent_block_for() (db_lookup.py:3747-3751) -- so a 'content' row with canonical_slot='text' promotes into a standalone sgs/text child block exactly the same way a 'text-content' row does; the promotion is role-agnostic among content-bearing roles, not text-content-exclusive. The ONE place the two are NOT interchangeable: converter/resolvers/array_content.py:249-254's L1d leaf-item text self-extraction fallback checks `frole == "text-content"` only, so a flat/leaf array-item field declared role='content' does not get that fallback (it would concatenate a structured item's children if it did; a leaf has none, so the exclusion is conservative, not a proven bug).
core: WP-core-block reference data (block_attributes.source='native_wp' -- rows seeded by the dbschema/ WP-reference-archive tooling for audit-feature-parity.py comparisons, never a cloning-pipeline input). ADDED 2026-08-13 (Bean, DB role-remediation part 2) as the first role to use the schema's third, previously-unused `classification` bucket -- 'unclassified', not 'content-bearing' or 'styling-behaviour', because a native_wp row is compared against an sgs/* block's feature set, it is never walked, extracted, or CSS-routed by the converter. Seeded structurally by TIER 3.18 in assign-canonical.py (`WHERE role IS NULL AND source = 'native_wp'`), never by name or block-slug guessing. Closed 225 of the 479 role-IS-NULL rows measured live 2026-08-13 -- every one of them had css_property IS NULL, confirming this population was invisible to every css_property-keyed tier by construction, not by oversight.
enum-class-probe: A BEM `--modifier` class carries this attr's value (a variant/style selector expressed only as a modifier suffix on the draft element, never as a CSS declaration). Consumer: converter/db/db_lookup.py:4889-4896 scans a block's attrs for role IN (select-from-enum, enum-class-probe, behaviour) whose derived_selector or canonical_slot ends with `--<modifier>`, then matches it against the draft's actual BEM modifier class.

enum-class-probe.excludes_reason: The matched consumer (db_lookup.py:4916) writes the LITERAL MODIFIER STRING into the attr (`result[attr_name] = modifier`) -- a string value, unconditionally. A boolean attr fed that string is a type-shape mismatch (WP coerces an out-of-schema value to the attr's default, per feedback_blockjson_enum_coerces_invalid_to_default). Found live 2026-08-05 (D497 follow-up, TIER 3.7): sgs/business-info|notice-banner.showIcon, sgs/cart.hideOnCartCheckoutPages -- plain editor toggles with no BEM-modifier signal at all (derived_selector/canonical_slot both NULL). See assign-canonical.py TIER 3.7.

icon-dashicon: Icon-source value: a Dashicons name (e.g. sgs/icon.dashiconName). CONSUMER (corrected 2026-08-05 — the previous text claimed 'NO consumer in the converter' for all four icon-* roles and that was WRONG): converter/services/extraction.py:1110-1116 builds `icon_source_attrs` from EVERY attr whose role starts with 'icon-', then `icon_source_attrs.get('icon-' + kind)` binds the kind resolved by resolve_icon_kind() (field_extractors.py:100-142) to its target attr. Shipped at D263 (2026-07-03), live-verified on page 8. WHY THE OLD CLAIM LOOKED TRUE: it cited field_extractors.py:201-213, the icon-resolver's fixed priority chain, which genuinely never branches on the role — but that is not the consumer. A file-scoped read of one function concluded absence for the whole codebase. PROVEN BY EXPERIMENT 2026-08-05: acting on that claim, the icon-lucide/icon-dashicon/icon-wp-icon declarations were retired so the Tier-1 name regex claimed those attrs as 'identity'; that dropped them out of this dispatch and broke test_icon_leaf_lifts_lucide_slug / _dashicon_by_kind / _wp_icon_by_kind. Restoring the three roles turned '3 failed, 3 passed' into '6 passed' with no other change. ⛔ DO NOT retire an icon-* role without first running `pytest scripts/converter/tests/test_extraction.py -k icon`.

identity: Dual-purpose per caller, both content-bearing. (a) On a plain string attr, the block's identifying TEXT (e.g. productName) -- routed through the text-content extractor via converter/walk.py:277-289 (_typed_value_for_role: `role == "identity" and attr_type == "string"` -> extract_field_value(el, "text-content", ...)`), explicitly NOT the field_extractors 'identity' branch (that would mean icon-slug resolution -- an unrelated overloaded semantic, converter/context.py:277-283). (b) On an icon-source leaf, 'identity' is grouped with 'icon-slug' in the icon priority-chain resolver (converter/services/field_extractors.py:207-213) and in converter/resolvers/array_content.py:168-169's _FLAT_SELF_ROLES (a flat item, e.g. a social-icon <a>, may self-extract this role). Content-bearing per _content_bearing_roles() (db_lookup.py:3744), so it also participates in Tier-A canonical_slot promotion.
image-alt: Alt text for a sibling image-object attr (e.g. sgs/product-card.imageAlt, sgs/media.imageAlt). Content-bearing display value the cloning image arm lifts alongside the image URL, not a styling property. The specific image attr it belongs to is named by block_attributes.alt_companion_attr, resolved by image_alt_companion_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:2611-2636, queries `role = 'image-alt' AND alt_companion_attr = ?`) and consumed at converter/walk.py:485 -- never guessed by name-parsing.
image-object: Scalar media/image value: an {url,id,alt} object, or (for a string-typed image-object attr) the bare URL string. Consumer: the Tier-A canonical_slot join in equivalent_block_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:3744-3751, gated content-bearing) for InnerBlock promotion (e.g. sgs/icon.iconSource -> child sgs/icon); converter/resolvers/scalar_content.py:172 is_media_object lift for block-private scalar image attrs (e.g. sgs/team-member's photo); converter/services/field_extractors.py:189-193 resolves the dict/URL from the matched element's descendant.
layout: Marks a structural/spacing attr -- explicitly NOT content-bearing. converter/db/db_lookup.py:3841-3844: a row with canonical_slot='content' + role='layout' routes its CSS value to the PARENT's own contentPadding* attrs, never emitted as a child InnerBlock (e.g. sgs/hero.contentPaddingTop). Also grouped into the shared px-unit CSS-kind inference at _kind_for() (db_lookup.py:1955-1957).
link-href: An href/URL value. Consumer: converter/services/field_extractors.py:248-253 extracts the nearest <a href> (sanitised via _safe_href); converter/resolvers/array_content.py:168-169's _FLAT_SELF_ROLES lets a flat item (e.g. a bare social-icon <a>) self-extract its own href; converter/services/extraction.py:1069-1070 gates the single-leaf lift's 'ONE url' arm on `role in ("link-href", "url-href")`.
motion: A transition/animation-duration-shaped CSS value. Consumer: grouped into the shared px-unit CSS-kind inference at _kind_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1955-1957) alongside layout/typography/visual/spacing/shadow/number-css-px -- no motion-specific branch exists beyond that shared unit classification.
number-css-percent: A numeric CSS value whose native unit is %. Consumer: _kind_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1959-1960) resolves it to CSS kind 'number_px' -- the % suffix is stripped the same way px is, since the wrapper re-applies the correct unit at emit time.
number-css-px: A numeric CSS value whose native unit is px. Consumer: grouped into the shared px-unit CSS-kind inference at _kind_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1955-1957).

number-css-px.excludes_reason: 'Numeric value whose native unit is px' cannot be a two-state boolean. Found live 2026-08-05 (D497 follow-up, TIER 3.7): sgs/mega-panel.bgBlur is a plain ON/OFF blur toggle, css_property NULL -- no px value exists on the attr at all. See assign-canonical.py TIER 3.7.

position: Stacking-context / positioning value (e.g. sgs/decorative-image.zIndex, css_property='z-index') -- a layout-positioning property, not content. Added 2026-07-15 (F6: enrichment derived the role before its roles row existed; the D128 scalar-media class of gap). CONSUMER NOTE (2026-08-04): no converter code branches on the literal 'position' anywhere -- zIndex's value transfers via the generic css_property join, not a role-specific check. Beyond zIndex, the wider position/inset/top/right/bottom/left family has property_suffixes rows seeded (D250) but 'NO block currently declares a matching attr for any of these six' (converter/resolvers/outer_box.py:43-46) -- a prepared-but-unused CSS destination family, honest NO_DESTINATION gap rather than a bug.
rating: Star/numeric rating value (e.g. sgs/testimonial.ratingStars) -- a content-bearing display value, not a styling property. Consumer: converter/resolvers/scalar_content.py:122,165 (is_rating: role == 'rating' and attr_type == 'number' -> star-count lift via aria-label/glyph count); converter/resolvers/array_content.py:168-169's _FLAT_SELF_ROLES also lets a flat array item self-extract a rating role (L1c).
scalar-media: A composite's own built-in scalar media SLOT (e.g. sgs/hero.splitImage/splitImageMobile) -- distinct from image-object: it marks a composite-interior COLUMN that must be lifted as a scalar object attr rather than folded as bare InnerBlocks. Consumer: has_scalar_media_attrs()/scalar_media_attr_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:2842-2874, FR-31-19) gate _route_composite_interior's routing decision, joined via block_attributes.role='scalar-media' + the slots aliases -- no per-block slug literal. Classified styling-behaviour (excluded from the generic content walk) DELIBERATELY: it is routed by this dedicated composite-interior mechanism instead, and check_row_floor.py pins sgs/hero's splitImage/splitImageMobile rows as a VALUE_ASSERTION because this role flipped to 'image-object' once already, silently breaking art-directed (mobile/desktop) image cropping.
select-from-enum: A string CSS value chosen from a fixed enum (e.g. font-style: italic/normal). Consumer: _kind_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1964-1965) resolves it to CSS kind 'string'; also grouped into the BEM-modifier probe at db_lookup.py:4889-4896 alongside enum-class-probe/behaviour.

select-from-enum.excludes_reason: The contract promises 'a string CSS value chosen from a fixed enum' -- both wired consumers (_kind_for's CSS-kind resolution, the BEM-modifier probe's literal-string write) expect a string/number VALUE, never a two-state flag. Numeric enums (e.g. font-weight steps) are a legitimate CSS value shape and stay admitted -- only boolean is excluded. Found live 2026-08-05 (D497 follow-up, TIER 3.7): 9 boolean rows -- sgs/countdown-timer.evergreenMode (plain mode toggle, no css_property, no draft signal -> 'boolean-visibility') and 8 image-effect toggles across card-grid/gallery/info-box/post-grid/team-member (imageZoomHover/grayscaleHover, css_property='transform'/'filter' legitimately set for INPUT-side routing -- the css_property lets the converter match a draft's filter:grayscale()/transform declaration onto the toggle, but the toggle's OWN value is never itself that CSS value; the actual value is hardcoded in the block's preset stylesheet -> new role 'css-gate', not 'boolean-visibility', because 'boolean-visibility' promises NO CSS signal exists and that would be false for these rows). See assign-canonical.py TIER 3.7 and the 'css-gate' role entry below.

spacing-token: A design-token-backed spacing value. Consumer: _kind_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1966-1968) lifts ONLY the BlockGap suffix (gap: Npx, a single CSS property) as CSS kind 'number_px'; the Spacing suffix (a padding/margin preset, multi-property) is deliberately NOT CSS-lifted through this path.
styling: Generic STYLING attribute: the row carries a non-NULL css_property, so a structural mechanism has already proven it paints CSS, but no more specific styling family (layout / color / typography / visual / motion / position) was established for it. Classification 'styling-behaviour' keeps it OUT of the content walk, exactly like those specific families. ADDED 2026-08-05 (Bean) to end the ambiguity of a bare NULL: before this, 109 sgs/% rows had a css_property AND role IS NULL, which reads identically to 'nobody has looked at this yet' and sent repeated sessions re-investigating rows that were already understood. WHY GENERIC RATHER THAN DERIVED: 81 of 90 distinct css_property values do map to exactly one role elsewhere in the table, but only 53 of the 109 had any precedent at all, and a precedent-derived role is inference from OTHER rows' classifications, not evidence about THIS row -- it would also be self-referential at seed time, so one wrong row could cascade. This role claims only what is proven: it is styling. Assigned by assign-canonical.apply_role_detection_inline() as a structurally-LAST pass, so it can never pre-empt a content-bearing verdict. SECOND EVIDENCE ROUTE ADDED 2026-08-06 (Bean): a row whose ONLY consumer anywhere in the plugin is includes/class-sgs-container-wrapper.php also earns this role, via TIER 2.4 (_apply_wrapper_styling_tier), even though its css_property is NULL. The wrapper is a CSS-rendering engine end to end -- everything it reads off the attributes bag it reads in order to paint a declaration -- so a wrapper-only read is styling BY CONSTRUCTION, the same positive-evidence standard the 'technical' role takes from a D1 veto. Those rows carry no css_property and never will: the emission scanner reads each block's own render.php/style.css and never the shared wrapper, and sgs/container -- the block every composite mirrors (R-31-9) -- deliberately declines to map the decorative families (overlayGradient*/shapeDivider*/bgSvg*) in its `decorative` element. Bean's governing rule: a NULL role means the row is UNREACHED or UNSEEDABLE, never 'reached, understood, and filed nowhere'. Measured 2026-08-06: 33 such rows, disjoint from every other verdict set.
svg: Raw inline SVG markup (sgs/hero.svgContent, sgs/media.svgContent, and the four bgSvgContent attrs consumed by includes/class-sgs-container-wrapper.php:458). CONTENT-BEARING with its own extractor branch at converter/services/field_extractors.py (role == 'svg'), which returns the <svg> element's MARKUP. It exists because routing SVG through the text branch is ACTIVELY DESTRUCTIVE, not merely imprecise: rich_text_content() keeps only a text-tag whitelist, so <svg>/<path>/<g> are stripped and a real icon arrives as the empty string -- these attrs carried role='content' and would have been mangled the moment a draft matched. Distinct from the icon-* roles and from 'identity': those resolve an <svg> to a NAMED library icon SLUG via icon_resolver; this returns the bespoke markup itself, which has no slug. Added 2026-08-05 (Bean) as a 3-part build -- role + extractor branch + reclassification in one change -- deliberately NOT as a bare DB relabel, because four icon-* roles in this table already have no consumer and do nothing.
tag-identity: The attr stores the source element's HTML tag (sgs/heading.level, sgs/media.mediaType). R-31-2 shape fact written by assembly step 3a2 (converter/services/assembly.py:160), gated on enum membership and read back via converter/db/db_lookup.py:1110-1125. Structural identity, never content-walked (classified styling-behaviour on purpose).

tag-identity.excludes_reason: An HTML tag name (h1..h6, div, span...) is inherently a string/enum value -- a boolean cannot store it. Zero live rows carry this pairing today (verified 2026-08-05, D497 follow-up, TIER 3.7); recorded pre-emptively from the contract text alone, same reasoning class as select-from-enum/colour-gradient/enum-class-probe/number-css-px above, so a future writer that DID map a boolean here would be caught rather than silently accepted.

technical: Generic TECHNICAL attribute: a machine-facing value -- a form-processing key, an element id or cross-block reference, a link `rel`, a taxonomy/query key, an enum dispatch key. Classification 'styling-behaviour' keeps it OUT of the content walk (it is not client-authored copy and a draft mockup carries no signal it could be lifted from). ADDED 2026-08-05 (Bean), symmetric with the 'styling' role added the same day and for the same reason: a bare NULL cannot distinguish 'nobody has examined this' from 'examined, and it is a backend key'. Both readings sent repeated sessions re-investigating settled rows. EVIDENCE REQUIRED -- this role is assigned ONLY from a Detector-1 VETO: D1 walked every usage site of the attribute in render.php/includes and found NONE content-bearing (each verdict NOT-content or value-fragment). That is positive evidence of what the value does, not an inference from its name. Rows that no detector reached are NOT given this role; they stay NULL, because 'unreached' and 'proven technical' are different facts and collapsing them would be the exact ambiguity this role exists to remove. Assigned by assign-canonical.apply_role_detection_inline() after the content tiers and before the 'styling' backstop, so any content verdict and any css_property both take precedence.
text-content: Rich-text content value -- extracted via rich_text_content (converter/services/field_extractors.py:182-184). 'content' (see that entry) is a first-class alias for every extraction path except one: converter/resolvers/array_content.py:249-254's L1d leaf-item self-extraction fallback checks `frole == "text-content"` specifically, so only a text-content-role field on a flat/leaf array item gets that fallback. The Tier-A canonical_slot->standalone_block promotion into a child sgs/text InnerBlock (db_lookup.py:3747-3751, worked example at db_lookup.py:5650-5651) is role-agnostic among content-bearing roles -- 'content' rows promote identically when canonical_slot matches -- so text-content is the more common spelling for this role, not an exclusive licence.
typography: A font/type CSS value (font-size, line-height, font-family, letter-spacing, etc.). Consumer: grouped into the shared px-unit CSS-kind inference at _kind_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1955-1957); no typography-specific branch exists beyond that shared unit classification.
visual: A generic visual/effects CSS value (opacity, box-shadow, and similar). Consumer: grouped into the shared px-unit CSS-kind inference at _kind_for() (converter/db/db_lookup.py:1955-1957); converter/resolvers/outer_box.py:82,307 additionally give role='color' priority over role='visual' when both resolve to the same box-shadow destination attr (rowid-ordering tie-break, e.g. Shadow vs BoxShadow).
enum-mode: An author-picked MODE KEY: the value is one of a fixed list DECLARED in the block's block.json `enum`, and it selects WHICH BRANCH RENDERS -- a CSS rule set, a markup arrangement, or a dispatch path. The value is NOT necessarily itself a CSS value. SEEDED DETERMINISTICALLY (assign-canonical.py TIER 3.5) from `enum_values IS NOT NULL`, which /sgs-update Stage 1 reads straight out of block.json (sgs-update-v2.py:895) -- so this role is a structural fact about the schema, never a name guess. WHY IT IS NOT `select-from-enum`: that role's contract is 'a string CSS VALUE chosen from a fixed enum' and it is wired into two consumers that rely on that promise -- _kind_for() (db_lookup.py:1964-1965) resolves it to CSS kind 'string', and the BEM-modifier probe (db_lookup.py:4889-4896) may WRITE a draft's modifier into it. Most enum attrs are not CSS values at all (sgs/card-grid.source = manual|query|wc-product; sgs/container.tagName; sgs/audio.audioSource), so filing them there would feed both consumers a falsehood. `enum-mode` is deliberately in NEITHER consumer group. GENERIC AND UPGRADEABLE, by design: it is classification='styling-behaviour' (so the row is excluded from the content walk -- walk.py's _typed_value_for returns None for it) but it is NOT 'graduated' in resolve_role_with_healing(), so the moment property_suffixes can resolve the attr to a specific family (typography/color/layout/visual...) the healer OVERWRITES this role automatically. e.g. sgs/container.backgroundRepeat carries this today and should become `visual` + css_property='background-repeat' once a suffix reaches it. WHAT IT PROTECTS (Bean, 2026-08-05): role IS NULL must mean ONE thing -- 'no seeding mechanism reached this row'. Leaving a row NULL merely because no role fitted destroys that signal and makes an unexamined row indistinguishable from an examined one, which is the same argument that keeps `technical` narrow (see its entry).
css-gate: A BOOLEAN attr whose own value is NEVER itself a CSS value -- it only GATES whether a companion css_property applies. The property's actual value lives elsewhere (hardcoded in the block's own preset stylesheet, e.g. card-grid/style.css:233-254's `.sgs-card-grid--zoom-hover:hover img{transform:scale(1.05)}`), and block_attributes.css_property is set on the boolean PURELY for INPUT-side routing: it lets the cloning converter match a draft's raw `filter: grayscale(...)`/`transform: scale(...)` CSS declaration onto this toggle during extraction (the SAME css_property join every other role uses for OUTPUT routing, here repurposed one-directionally for INPUT). ADDED 2026-08-05 (Bean, D497 follow-up / TIER 3.7) for exactly the class of row `select-from-enum` could not honestly hold: sgs/card-grid|gallery|post-grid|team-member.imageZoomHover (css_property='transform') and sgs/card-grid|gallery|info-box|team-member.grayscaleHover (css_property='filter'). WHY NOT 'boolean-visibility' -- that role's own contract states 'a draft's HTML/CSS carries no signal a boolean toggle could be lifted from, so the absence of a resolver is expected, not a gap'; that claim is FALSE for these rows (there is a real css_property-driven input signal), so filing them there would misdocument a working mechanism as absent. WHY NOT 'select-from-enum' -- its two consumers (_kind_for's CSS-kind resolution, the BEM-modifier probe's literal-string write, both converter/db/db_lookup.py) expect a STRING/NUMBER CSS value; writing either into a boolean attr is the exact type-shape mismatch this role exists to prevent. Do NOT clear or alter the row's css_property when assigning this role -- css_property is CORRECT here, only the role was wrong (assign-canonical.py TIER 3.7 asserts this: it never touches css_property, role only).
link-content: A CONCATENATED FRAGMENT of a URL the block assembles around it -- not a whole href. Consumer: converter/services/field_extractors.py extract_link_fragment() (dispatched from extract_field_value's `role == "link-content"` branch), fed the block's captured URL template by converter/db/db_lookup.py link_template_for(), which reads block_attributes.output_signature's `link_template` key (written by scripts/behavioural-analyser/extract-signatures.py _detect_link_template, commit 580f7885). Two call paths supply it: converter/walk.py NESTED leg 1b (root-self -- the block's OWN root <a href>, which is where sgs/whatsapp-cta's phoneNumber and message both live, since render.php:54-58 builds 'https://wa.me/' . $clean_phone then .= '?text=' . rawurlencode($message)) and converter/walk.py _typed_value_for_role (the descendant-element sibling, for a block whose link hangs off a BEM-tokened child). WHY IT IS NOT link-href: every other content-bearing role extracts a WHOLE value, so storing the assembled href in phoneNumber would have render.php re-prefix it into 'https://wa.me/httpswame447700900123texthi' -- a corrupted client phone number that still LOOKS like a successful clone. The template is what makes the round trip reversible. FAIL-CLOSED BY DESIGN: no captured template, no single {value} placeholder, no scheme-allowlisted href, or an href that does not carry the template's literals -> None, never a guessed fragment. Fragment boundaries are the URL's own RFC 3986 delimiters (path fragment ends at ?/#, query fragment at &/#) and percent-decoding is applied to a QUERY fragment only, being the exact inverse of the rawurlencode() the assembling render applies. Added 2026-08-06 as role + extractor + threading in ONE change, mirroring the 'svg' role's 3-part build: a DB-only role flip leaves the value silently returning None.
css-modifier: The BEM --<modifier> suffix on an element's own class list (e.g. `sgs-testimonial__rating--scale` -> 'scale'), read verbatim as a string enum value. Reachable via extract_field_value's generic role dispatch (converter/services/field_extractors.py:487-493) and unit-tested in test_field_extractors.py. First real DB adopter is sgs/testimonial.ratingType (added 2026-09-05). Consumer (scalar path): converter/resolvers/scalar_content.py lift_scalar_content()'s is_css_modifier check (role=='css-modifier' and attr_type=='string') -- resolves a block's own modifier-driven enum (e.g. ratingType 'stars'|'scale', set by the same element a sibling numeric-content/rating attr also matches) from draft content rather than staying stuck at its block.json default.
numeric-content: A genuinely NUMERIC (decimal-capable) content value read verbatim from an element's text -- e.g. sgs/testimonial.ratingScale, a continuous 0-100 review score ('9.2 / 10'), which is NOT an enum pick and is NOT a 0-5 star count. Added 2026-09-05 (Task 4 testimonial audit) because neither existing numeric-shaped role fit: 'rating' (converter/services/field_extractors.py role=='rating' branch) hardcodes extract_star_count(), which reads an aria-label digit or counts star glyphs and clamps to 0..5 -- correct for a star count, silently wrong (data-corrupting, not merely absent) for any wider numeric range; 'select-from-enum' is for a fixed choice set the attr's value is drawn from, and a continuous score is not a choice. Consumer: converter/services/field_extractors.py extract_field_value() role=='numeric-content' branch -- regex-matches the FIRST signed decimal token in the matched element's text (get_text()) and returns it as a Python float, or None when no numeric token is present (never a guessed value). Gate: converter/resolvers/scalar_content.py lift_scalar_content()'s is_numeric check (role=='numeric-content' and attr_type=='number'). Universal: any future block with a genuinely-numeric scalar text field (not a star count, not an enum) uses this role rather than inventing a bespoke one.
presence-boolean: A boolean whose TRUE value is signalled by the mere PRESENCE of a matched draft element -- e.g. sgs/testimonial.verified, where a review is 'verified' precisely when the draft renders its `.sgs-testimonial__verified` badge span at all (the badge's own text content is irrelevant; only whether the element exists). Added 2026-09-05 (Task 4 testimonial audit) to correct a genuine misclassification: 'verified' previously carried role='boolean-visibility', whose own contract states 'a draft's HTML/CSS carries no signal a boolean toggle could be lifted from, so the absence of a resolver is expected, not a gap' -- that claim is FALSE for this attr (the badge's presence/absence IS a real, unambiguous draft signal), so filing it under boolean-visibility misdocumented a genuinely liftable field as unliftable. Do NOT reclassify an editor-only preference toggle (e.g. avatarDecorative, orgLogoDecorative -- an operator's own alt-text override with no draft-side signal) to this role; those correctly stay 'boolean-visibility'. Consumer: converter/services/field_extractors.py extract_field_value() role=='presence-boolean' branch -- always returns True (the caller only invokes it once a derived_selector match has already been found; non-match already means no key is emitted, matching every other role's no-op floor). Gate: converter/resolvers/scalar_content.py lift_scalar_content()'s is_presence check (role=='presence-boolean' and attr_type=='boolean').
